examples.pie: ph₂tḗr toy h₂eh₂ógʰe? h₂eh₂ógʰe. ǵʰwḗr nos dwóyh₁ h₂ówih₁ gʷʰént. deywṓs h₁ésmey néwās h₂ówins dh₃ih₁ént.

examples.pie: h₂réh₁ǵtor toy h₂enterowékʷos h₁wésu. gʷr̥Htíns toy dédeh₃mi. téwe mówdos méne mówdos. néwom preḱnóm préḱsdʰi.
examples.en: Helper, your answer is good. I give you thanks. Your joy is my joy. Ask a new question!

examples.pie: kʷíd súpniyom? h₁yód nékʷti légʰesi ménos toy h₁éǵʰs h₁éyti néweh₂-kʷe spéḱyeti. tód súpniyom. wékʷesh₂ toy h₁sónth₂.

examples.pie: h₂stérm̥ widés h₁yós diwés péth₁t? h₁ím widóm. méǵh₂s h₂nḗr mért. kʷís só h₂nḗr? h₃rḗǵs nos ǵérh₂onts. h₁ésyo dṓm h₁éyoh₂? gʷh₂dʰí wékʷos-kʷe moy h₂éyeri sl̥ǵdʰí. kʷsépi h₂én drémoh₂.

examples.pie: h₁yód gʰrémesi th₂kéh₁ye. h₁yód toy ménos h₃reǵtóm nu bʰh₂dʰí. gʰrémontos wiHrósyo wékʷos ǵʰoysós. priHóm térh₃t.

examples.pie: léwbʰa h₂éwsos kʷséps téwe swésōr h₁ésti. kʷséps légʰt stéh₂s lówksneh₂ séngʷt wiHrṓs-kʷe bʰudʰént. ǵʰlóh₁onti h₂éwsos gʷm̥sḱési. h₂éwsos nos léwkm̥ h₁opéye.
examples.en: Dear Dawn, Night is your sister. Night lay down; you stood up. The moon sank, and the men woke. Dawn, shining, you come. Give us light, Dawn.

examples.pie: diwés dʰúgh₂ter ǵʰlóh₁esi. h₁yéh₂ kʷsépm̥ h₂epó h₂éǵesi. nu h₁yéh₂ dʰéǵʰōm lowkéyesi. h₁yéh₂ sóh₂wl̥ wédʰesi gʷéms h₂stéres n̥ḱént. h₂éwsos h₂ew h₁ludʰé sóh₂wl̥-kʷe nos wédʰe.
examples.en: Daughter of Sky, you shine. You who drive the night away, you who then light up the earth, you who bring the sun! You came; the stars vanished. Come again, Dawn, and bring us the sun.

examples.pie: nu léwke dyéw h₁regʷesyéti. sóh₂wl̥ séngʷt h₂stéres-kʷe stesth₂ḗr. téwe-ge h₂stéres ǵʰlóh₁onti. nu téwe lówksneh₂ ǵʰlóh₁eti ph₂sdʰí nos. h₂éwsōs-ge téwe dʰugh₂tḗr h₂ew gʷm̥yóyh₁t.
examples.en: Now, bright Sky, it grows dark. The sun sank, and the stars are standing. Your stars indeed shine, now your moon shines. Protect us. May Dawn, your daughter, indeed come again.

source.note: Near deictic 'this (here)': Hitt. kā- < *ḱo- (Fortson §9.25; Beekes p. 227; Handbook ch. 21 §5.1), i-stem *ḱi- in OCS sь, Lith. šìs, Goth. himma, Lat. cis (Fortson §7.10; Handbook ch. 116 §5.1 *ḱis). Ringe 2017 p. 56 pairs adnominal *ḱo- with full-NP *ḱi/e- and says the o-stems inflect like the relative. Hittite-attested cells are cited; the rest follow demonstrative_so (see _derived). The i-stem is kept only as an alternative nom. sg. m. *ḱís.
